summary: Steve opens a new series in Galatians, noting it covers many of the same doctrinal themes as Romans in a shorter, more accessible way. After reading Galatians 1:1-5 aloud and praying, he walks through Paul's opening words. Paul begins by defending his authority as an apostle, since some in Galatia were trying to undermine his credibility by pointing to his past as a persecutor of the church. Paul insists his calling came directly from Jesus Christ and God the Father, not from any human appointment. Steve then turns to verse 2, "all the brethren who are with me," noting that Paul wrote alongside trusted companions -- likely including Barnabas -- and that believers need a community of faith around them. He gives historical background on Galatia, explaining that the name referred both to an ethnic Celtic people and, later, to a wider Roman province (including Lyconia, Phrygia, and Pisidia) where Paul had personally planted churches on his first missionary journey (Acts 13-14).

He closes by walking through verses 3-5 and summarizing the gospel: because of God's grace, Jesus lived a perfect life and died to take away the curse of sin, and it is faith in that finished work -- not human effort or credentials -- that saves.
takeaways: Your past mistakes or lack of formal credentials don't disqualify you from what God is calling you to do -- what matters is obedience to that calling, not other people's opinions of your past.
Surround yourself with a real community of faith, people who will encourage you and hold you accountable to the truth, the way Paul surrounded himself with trusted companions.

Don't wait passively for direction -- move in the direction you believe God is leading, trusting Him to redirect you if needed, the way He redirected Paul on the road to Damascus. The gospel is simple at its core: because of grace, Christ died for our sins, and faith in Him - not works or pedigree -- is what saves us. Hold to the truth you've already been taught, even when others try to pull you away from it.
